_note: PLAN.md 9. All numbers are STARTING VALUES to be tuned by playtest --
balance is ours to design, not inherited from any reference game.
Units: speed is SUB-UNITS PER TICK (SimUnit.speed, PLAN.md 6.2) at
SimWorld.SUBTILE per tile and 10 ticks/second. gather_rate is per 100 ticks,
so 25 means a quarter of a unit per tick -- authored x100 to keep the sim on
integers, because a float leaking into it breaks determinism (PLAN.md 7.1).
THE FULL ROSTER, added once all 19 unit bakes landed. Every speed below is
the villager's base scaled by the unit's relative pace, so the whole roster
moves consistently the moment that one number is retuned.
EVERY SPEED WAS HALVED ON 2026-08-23, on the project owner's instruction
after a real session: 'if we reduce the unit speed by 50% making them half
as slow as they are now'. This closes the oldest and most valuable item in
BUGS.md -- 'every unit feels too fast', owner-reported 2026-08-21 from a
two-device match on a phone -- which was deliberately parked until it could
be done as ONE pass over the whole roster rather than a nudge to whichever
unit was on screen. This is that pass. The villager went 200 -> 100 and
every other unit was scaled by the same half, so the relative pacing the
paragraph above describes is untouched; only the absolute pace moved.
Odd values rounded away from zero (175 -> 88, 125 -> 63), because the sim
carries no floats. The four speed 0 units below stayed 0 -- see the next
paragraph, that zero means 'has no walk clip', not 'slow'.
WHAT THIS DID NOT FIX, and was expected to. The same report said chopping,
mining and wildlife attacks repeated about twice too fast, and reasoned that
speed was the shared cause. It is not: while a unit holds a work or attack
animation, how often its sound plays is set by `throttle_ms`/`crowd_ms` in
data/audio.json and by nothing else -- a stationary villager chopping is
unaffected by how fast she walks. Those rates were retuned separately in the
same session (tools/stage_audio.py carries the arithmetic). Recorded here
because the two symptoms arrived together and will look related again.
UNITS DO NOT CARRY THE AGE (PLAN.md 2.7): one actor in all four ages, and
no age-suffixed visual. What a unit DOES carry is `age_required`, the age
its trainer must have reached before it appears in that building's train
menu. That lives here rather than as four `trains` lists per building --
an archery range trains archers from age 2 and crossbowmen from age 3, and
expressing that on the unit means adding a unit touches one file.
FOUR UNITS HAVE speed 0, AND IT IS NOT A PLACEHOLDER. For the three siege
engines it now reads as the DEPLOYED speed, which is the number it always
was: a set-up engine does not move, and it bakes with idle and attack only,
so giving it a speed would slide a static sprite across the map. The dragon
has no armature in the source at all and cannot move until someone rigs it.
`packing` IS THE SECOND SPEED, added 2026-08-28 with `SiegeSystem` (PLAN.md
4.13). 0 A.D. ships each engine as a packed/unpacked actor PAIR, and the
packed one is the wagon it travels on -- idle and walk, 12 frames each, so
the walk clip that was missing exists after all, on the other actor. A unit
declaring `packing` travels folded up and fights set down, and the ticks are
the cost of changing between them at both ends.
`visual` IS THE SWITCH, exactly as `attack.projectile` is for a shot: no
packed art, no packing, and no rule infers it. `unit.siege_ram` is the case
that proves it -- a siege engine that walks at 63 with one actor, needing no
exception written for it.
Speeds are set against the ram's 63, the only other mobile siege: 55 / 50 /
40, heavier engines slower. Ticks are 3 / 5 / 8 seconds at SimClock's 10 a
second, on the same ladder. Both ends of a move pay, so shifting a trebuchet
two tiles is sixteen seconds of not shooting -- which is the point of the
feature and the reason the numbers are not smaller.
SHIPS ARE STATIC and carry domain `water`, so pathing already refuses to
walk them onto land. They have a speed because they are meant to move; what
they lack is a walk ANIMATION, so they will slide rather than row.
THE TRANSPORT CARRIES SIX, added 2026-08-29 with the Archipelago map type
(2.4d), and `garrison_cap` is deliberately the SAME KEY a building uses. A
boat holding six spearmen and a castle holding fifteen are one mechanism --
PLAN.md 4.8's garrison, which since 4.8 has stored an ENTITY id rather than a
building id -- so this needed a second reader and not a second feature.
Six, against the castle's 15 and a tower's 5. It is a landing party rather
than an army: two boats to move a real attack, which is what makes a navy
worth building rather than a formality on the way to one. It also costs 2
population itself, so ferrying is not free of the cap either.
WHAT STOPS A LANDING IN OPEN WATER is not a rule anybody wrote. Unloading
asks `find_free_adjacent` for a tile in the PASSENGER's domain, so infantry
come off onto land or do not come off at all -- and a transport in mid-ocean
simply refuses, keeping its cargo. The same line already handled a tower
walled in by its own owner.
ONLY THE VILLAGER GATHERS. The fishing ship has no gather_rate on purpose:
there is no fishing in the sim, and a non-empty gather_rate is what
SelectionActions reads as 'this is a worker' and would offer it a build
menu and a harvest verb it cannot act on.
BALLISTA AND ONAGER ARRIVED 2026-08-16 and complete the siege workshop.
They KEEP speed 0 alongside the trebuchet, and the reason has narrowed to
one thing: there is no walk clip, so a speed would slide a sprite that
cannot show itself walking. That is the whole of it -- and as of 2026-08-28
it is also the whole of why `packing` was the shape the fix had to take.
It used to say more, and the more was wrong. Both were first baked static on
the reasoning 'the source armature reports 0 bones, so no clip can attach'.
That premise was a bug in isobake's own inspector, which read armatures[0]
where the bake read subject_armature -- different objects on a composite
actor, because the crew import ahead of the engine. The ballista had 36
bones all along and now ships idle, attack, die and decay, 140 frames. So a
static siege engine was never a fact about siege engines; do not reason from
it again.
The ballista alone has no per-colour bake, and that DOES NOT generalise --
this note claimed it did and was wrong twice over. The siege ram tints (8
distinct pages) and so does the onager. Only the lithobolos art set measures
0%, re-confirmed after its crew were given their heads back. One actor, one
measurement, no rule. See visuals.json.
